stories.stat_label: years ago it roamed muddy wetlands
stories.headline: A dinosaur found in 2001 is a brand-new species
stories.summary: Dug from a Surrey brick quarry and kept at London's Natural History Museum, Paludohadros proudlovii was a rhino-sized young plant-eater, about 5 m long and up to 2 tonnes.
stories.why: It honours Will Proudlove, the quarry's manager, who died aged 35 shortly before it was dug up.

stories.stat_label: years the theory waited for proof
stories.headline: Diamond flaws just proved an 80-year-old physics theory
stories.summary: Using tiny quantum sensors inside a lab-grown diamond, a NIMS team mapped the stress around a single atomic flaw, about 10 times more precisely than older methods. It matched the theory.
stories.why: Better crystals could mean more reliable power and quantum devices.

stories.headline: Kew solved a 245-year mix-up over a famous medicinal mushroom
stories.summary: Since 1781, Europe's Ganoderma lucidum and East Asia's prized lingzhi, or reishi, were often treated as one. Old Kew specimens show they split at least 16 million years ago.
stories.why: The team proposes calling the European one 'false lingzhi', helping buyers know what they get.

stories.headline: Fishers raised the alarm, and 5 sea turtles swam free
stories.summary: Five female green sea turtles got caught in fish corrals. Local fishers reported them, and rescuers tagged and released them unhurt; the largest shell was 78 cm long.
stories.why: Green turtles are endangered, and quick reports from fishers are helping them survive.

fun_fact: The new dinosaur's name, Paludohadros, comes from 'palus', Latin for swamp.
